title: How the heating and cooling plant works
subtitle: A guided reading of Mes 600 S, revision 3
scope: Explanatory interpretation of the supplied design drawing. Equipment names and duties are design references; installation, commissioning and current settings have not been verified.
summary: Groundwater supplies or receives heat through two PC2 water-to-water heat pumps. Their building circuit provides winter heating and summer cooling.
A separate warm-water circuit from PC2 feeds the PC1 high-temperature heat pump. PC1 supplies the two SC1 heat exchangers that charge the domestic hot-water tanks.
Heat crosses exchanger surfaces. Groundwater, closed-loop heating water and potable water remain in separate circuits.
Distribution is divided into pressure zones. SC2 separates the high-pressure building circuit hydraulically from the main heating/cooling circuit.

modes.title: Winter heating
modes.lead: PC2 moves heat from groundwater into the building heating loop.
steps: Well P1 has two P11 pumps; well P2 is marked reserve and has one P10 pump. T6 and the two T7 filters protect the groundwater circuit; two S4 vessels stabilise pressure.
The two PC2 units raise the temperature of closed-loop water. The PC2 heating schedule gives 40 to 45 deg C on the user side and 16 to 11 deg C on the source side.

Two S3 buffers on the building circuit add thermal inertia. P06 serves Tower B communal spaces; P07 serves the low-pressure branches; P08 supplies SC2, with P09 circulating its separate high-pressure secondary circuit.

Apartment modules meter energy and mix the supplied water for radiant panels. Domestic hot water can also require the separate PC1 chain; the actual winter priority/staging sequence requires the control specification.
modes.caution: Groundwater mixing and some temperature annotations conflict with the equipment schedule. The values here explain the drawing; they are not commissioning instructions.

modes.title: Summer cooling
modes.lead: PC2 removes heat from the building; groundwater receives the rejected heat.
steps: Building return water gives up heat through PC2. Its cooling schedule states 15 to 10 deg C on the user side and 16 to 21 deg C on the source side.

The same distribution branches carry chilled water. The low- and high-pressure residential outlets are annotated 13/18 deg C; apartment mixing raises radiant-panel supply to 18 deg C, with a separate dehumidifier connection.

The MSW family supports cooling with hot-water recovery. In this scheme the separate 40/35 deg C circuit can supply PC1 while cooling demand exists; the installed controller must confirm the actual enable logic.
Groundwater flows back to the restitution wells through the temperature-control arrangement. The drawing describes different winter and summer mixing behaviour and manual seasonal changeover.
modes.caution: The main PC2 building pipes also show 8/13 deg C, and SC2 has another selection point. These are unresolved design annotations, not interchangeable settings. Condensation protection and humidity control need their own verified sequence.

modes.title: Domestic hot water
modes.lead: Two temperature stages charge two separate potable-water storage branches.
steps: PC2 supplies the intermediate 40/35 deg C circuit, which has two S3 buffers of 2,000 L each. P05 circulates this water through the source side of PC1.
PC1 uses electricity and intermediate-loop heat to deliver 70 deg C water, returning at 65 deg C. P04 circulates this high-temperature primary loop.

Two SC1 plate heat exchangers, each rated 90 kW in the drawing, transfer heat into two potable-water branches. Each P01 pump charges one S2 tank of 3,000 L; the potable charging circuit is labelled 60/55 deg C.

Each branch mixes stored hot water with cold water for a distribution annotation of 48 deg C. P02 and P03 circulate the medium- and low-pressure return loops respectively, limiting distribution cooling between draw-offs.
modes.caution: The 48 deg C labels do not demonstrate Legionella control or safe temperature at every outlet. T3 dosing is shown, but chemicals, dosing rates, hygiene programme and verification results are absent.

modes.title: Cooling + hot-water recovery
modes.lead: Heat removed from occupied spaces can help produce domestic hot water.
steps: The manufacturer's MSW family literature describes simultaneous cooling and hot-water production for its two-pipe multipurpose version.
The drawing provides PC2 with separate building, warm-water and groundwater connections. This topology is consistent with recovering cooling heat into the intermediate circuit.
PC1 then lifts the intermediate temperature for SC1 and the S2 tanks. This additional lift still consumes electricity.
Groundwater balances the source/sink requirement. The split between recovered and rejected heat depends on concurrent loads and the installed refrigeration and control configuration.
modes.caution: This is a supported family capability and a plausible reading of the topology. Simultaneous output, priority logic and seasonal efficiency are not established by the supplied drawing.

components.name: Main heating/cooling heat pumps
components.role: Exchange heat with groundwater; serve the building loop and a separate warm-water circuit feeding PC1.
components.design: Per unit: heating 260.4 kW / electrical input 53.3 kW, COP 4.88; cooling 233.3 kW / input 33.3 kW, EER 7.00. Separate hot-water mode output: 267.7 kW.
components.note: The downloaded MSW brochure describes the family, not the exact MSW182ML selection. Do not add the different mode ratings as simultaneous capacity, or treat their arithmetic sum across two units as guaranteed plant output.

components.name: High-temperature heat pump
components.location: p.1, centre: PC1 between DHW branches and intermediate buffers
components.role: Takes heat from the 40/35 deg C intermediate loop and supplies the 70/65 deg C SC1 primary loop.
components.design: 180.5 kW thermal; 37 kW total absorbed; two scroll compressors. Drawing states COP 5.00.
components.note: 180.5 / 37 = 4.88, which differs from the printed COP. The current KSW brochure explains the high-temperature function but does not validate this exact configured unit.

components.name: Thermal buffer tanks
components.role: Add thermal inertia in two distinct closed-water circuits, helping absorb short-term differences between generation and demand.
components.design: Each 2,000 L, nominal pressure 6 bar.
components.note: The repeated tag S3 identifies four drawn vessels. The intermediate and building water circuits are separate. These are thermal water buffers; their role differs from the S4 pressure vessels.

components.name: Domestic hot-water heat exchangers
components.location: p.1, left of PC1, next to the two S2 tanks
components.role: Transfer heat from PC1's closed primary loop to potable water without mixing the two fluids.
components.design: Each 90 kW; primary 70/65 deg C; potable secondary 60/55 deg C.
components.note: Heat-exchanger material, potable-water suitability, actual selection and inspection records require the installed documentation.

components.name: Domestic hot-water storage
components.location: p.1, centre-left, medium- and low-pressure DHW branches
components.role: Store heated potable water and buffer short peaks in draw-off.
components.design: Each 3,000 L, nominal pressure 10 bar; storage annotation 60 deg C.
components.note: The two downstream mixed outlets and recirculation lines are annotated 48 deg C. Storage capacity totals 6,000 L; usable draw-off depends on temperatures, stratification and recharge.

components.name: High-pressure zone heat exchanger
components.location: p.1, upper right between P08 and P09
components.role: Transfers heating or cooling across a hydraulic pressure boundary. P08 and P09 circulate different sides.
components.design: Winter 231 kW: primary 45/40 deg C, secondary 42.5/39 deg C. Summer 240 kW: primary 10/15 deg C, secondary 13/16.6 deg C.
components.note: Nearby distribution pipes instead show 42/38 and 13/18 deg C. The exchanger is a pressure-separation device; it does not itself boost pressure.

components.name: DHW charging circulators
components.location: p.1, each SC1 secondary / S2 charging loop
components.role: Circulate potable water from the storage charging connection through SC1 and back to S2.
components.design: Per schedule: 16 m3/h; 50 kPa head; 0.75 kW.
components.note: The DCM-GE family document explains inverter-driven circulation. Exact designation and wetted-material suitability for this potable circuit must be confirmed; the drawing allows equivalent equipment.

components.name: Medium-pressure DHW recirculation pump
components.model: DAB EVOPLUS B120/220.32 SAN M or equivalent
components.role: Returns water from the medium-pressure hot-water circulation loop to its charging/mixing arrangement.
components.note: The exact base SAN designation appears in the EVOPLUS manual, PDF p.2. This establishes model coverage, not the installed operating point.

components.name: Low-pressure DHW recirculation pump
components.model: DAB EVOPLUS B120/220.32 SAN M or equivalent
components.role: Maintains circulation in the low-pressure domestic hot-water return loop.
components.note: Recirculation reduces waiting time and temperature decay; it does not by itself establish adequate hygiene throughout the network.

components.name: PC1 hot-side circulator
components.role: Circulates the closed 70/65 deg C primary water between PC1 and the two SC1 branches.
components.note: DCM-GE 65-1200 family selection appears in the downloaded technical sheet, PDF p.28; actual suffix and curve must be checked.

components.name: PC1 source-side circulator
components.role: Circulates the intermediate warm-water loop through PC1's source exchanger.
components.design: 26 m3/h; 50 kPa; 0.75 kW; drawing lists 11.8 A.
components.note: The electrical current appears inconsistent with the listed power and comparable schedule entries; retain it as an unresolved source value.

components.name: Communal-space distribution circulator
components.role: Serves the Tower B communal-space heating/cooling branch.
components.note: No exact product document verified. The DPE designation is retained exactly as drawn, without assigning an unrelated product family.

components.name: Low-pressure zone circulator
components.role: Serves low-pressure heating/cooling outlets for Towers A and B through the drawn mixing arrangement.
components.note: Family-level reference only; the drawing's designation and selected curve need confirmation.

components.name: SC2 primary circulator
components.role: Moves main-loop water through the primary side of SC2.
components.note: The corresponding DCM-GE designation is covered on PDF p.34 of the technical sheet.

components.name: High-pressure zone circulator
components.role: Circulates SC2 secondary water to the high-pressure heating/cooling outlets for Towers A and B.
components.note: The installation manual covers the DCP-GE family; exact hydraulic selection is unverified.

components.name: Reserve-well submersible pump
components.model: DAB SS8 A05 + TR650 DIR PE2 or equivalent
components.role: Lifts groundwater from reserve extraction well P2 into the common source-water line.
components.note: SS-family manual explains the pump type; exact pump/motor pairing, yield and reserve changeover are unverified.

components.name: Main-well submersible pumps
components.model: DAB SS6 E11 + TR630 DIR PE2 or equivalent
components.role: Supply the normal extraction-well line feeding T6, T7 and PC2.
components.design: Each 54 m3/h = 15 L/s; 930 kPa; 22 kW.
components.note: Two pumps total 108 m3/h by arithmetic; this is not evidence of permitted combined abstraction with the reserve well.

components.name: Groundwater hydrocyclone
components.role: Uses swirling flow to separate heavier suspended particles before downstream filtration.
components.design: 108 m3/h; maximum pressure 8 bar in the drawing.
components.note: Candidate NIC 108-K reference matches DN125 and 108 m3/h but specifies 6 bar, not 8 bar. Exact identity and pressure rating remain unverified.

components.name: Groundwater fine filters
components.role: Retain finer suspended particles before the heat pumps; pressure gauges support checking filter loading.
components.design: 65 m3/h each; 100 micrometres; 16 bar; 10 W as drawn.
components.note: Candidate ML100 literature states 60 m3/h and 30 W, with pressure limits depending on version. It explains a possible filter technology but does not identify the installed filters.

components.name: Groundwater pressure vessels
components.role: Provide a compliant water/air volume that helps stabilise pressure and reduce pump cycling.
components.design: Each 1,000 L; nominal pressure 10 bar.
components.note: DL-CE brochure describes replaceable-bladder vessels and includes DL 1000/10 CE. It is a distributor-hosted family reference; actual code and precharge must be confirmed. Gross volume is not usable draw-off volume.

components.name: Extraction and restitution wells
components.model: P1 main, P2 reserve; two restitution details both labelled R1
components.role: Provide an open groundwater source/sink circuit through PC2; return water to the aquifer. A branch also serves irrigation.
components.design: Restitution annotation: minimum discharge pressurisation > 0.5 bar. Source labels include 16 deg C supply, 11 deg C winter return and 21 deg C summer return.
components.note: Temperature/level dataloggers, sample points and a seasonal mixing arrangement are shown. Permitted rates, environmental limits and actual control settings are outside the supplied evidence.

components.name: Incoming potable-water filter
components.location: p.1, far left, incoming mains water
components.role: Removes suspended impurities before the potable-water storage and pressure-boosting arrangement.
components.design: 66 m3/h design flow in the drawing.
components.note: The official AMBRA DN100 sheet gives a 90 m3/h catalogue flow and 50-micrometre elements. A catalogue rating and a lower project duty can coexist; this is not automatically a conflict.

components.name: Pre-booster water vessels
components.role: Provide storage ahead of GP1/GP2; an air-management arrangement is also drawn.
components.design: Each 2,000 L; nominal pressure 8 bar.
components.note: Do not assume an ELBI S4-style bladder construction for these unspecified vessels.

components.name: Medium-pressure potable-water booster
components.role: Feeds the medium-pressure potable-water network, including its DHW feed branch.
components.design: Set flow 34 m3/h; head 730 kPa; schedule also states head setting 930 kPa; 2 x 7.5 kW.
components.note: The NKVE catalogue covers the 20/6 designation. Different head annotations and actual assembly selections require commissioning documents; do not treat them as instructions.

components.name: Low-pressure potable-water booster
components.role: Feeds the low-pressure potable-water network, including its DHW feed branch.
components.design: Set flow 37 m3/h; head 430 kPa; schedule also states head setting 630 kPa; 2 x 5.5 kW.
components.note: Use the drawing as the design record. Verify the installed pump, pressure-zone allocation and controls rather than inferring settings from a modern catalogue.

components.name: DHW-feed water softeners
components.location: p.1, left, ahead of T3/T4 and S2
components.role: Ion-exchange resin reduces hardness in the water feeding the DHW branches. A blending arrangement is drawn.
components.design: 13 m3/h; maximum 8 bar. Manufacturer /200 row: 200 L resin, 340 L brine vessel.
components.note: The catalogue confirms the /200 size on PDF p.2. The '0 degrees F' design annotation refers to French hardness degrees, not Fahrenheit or water temperature; final blended hardness is not established.

components.name: Anti-Legionella dosing equipment
components.model: Manufacturer, chemical and dosing regime not specified
components.role: Provides the treatment function labelled anti-Legionella in the drawing.
components.design: 50 W; 1 x 230 V per schedule.
components.note: Equipment presence alone does not establish treatment efficacy. An approved hygiene plan, chemical specification and monitoring results are needed.

components.name: Anticorrosion dosing equipment
components.location: p.1, treated DHW feeds alongside T3
components.role: Provides the anticorrosion treatment function identified by the designer.
components.design: 50 W; 1 x 230 V per schedule.
components.note: Potable-water compatibility, dosage and monitoring cannot be inferred from the generic dosing symbol.

components.name: Closed-loop water treatment
components.role: Treats make-up water for closed heating/cooling circuits. Automatic fill groups and backflow protection are drawn.
components.design: 50 W; 1 x 230 V per schedule.
components.note: Make-up connections are separate from normal heat-carrying circulation; treatment chemistry and target concentrations are unverified.

components.name: Plant control and metering
components.model: DDC K&P 4200; cascade controller; M-bus links
components.location: p.1, above PC2 and in bottom apartment details
components.role: Collects temperature/pressure information, commands regulated equipment, coordinates the heat-pump cascade and communicates metering data.
components.design: Outdoor sensor, manual summer/winter selector, GSM/Ethernet and alarms are drawn.
components.note: The drawing explicitly asks that control connections be checked with equipment suppliers. Exact controller documentation, sequences, interlocks and software have not been obtained.

components.name: Mixing, protection and service devices
components.location: p.1, all circuits and symbol legend
components.role: Mixing valves blend flows; check valves limit reverse flow; isolation valves permit service; expansion vessels accommodate volume changes; relief valves protect against overpressure; dirt separators capture debris.
components.design: Ratings differ by circuit and location. The emergency bypass near PC1 is labelled normally closed at its two valves.
components.note: These explanatory diagrams omit service details. No valve-operation, pressure-setting, chemical-dosing or bypass procedure is provided.

components.name: Apartment and communal-space modules
components.quantity: Typical details, not an installed count
components.role: Apartments combine metering, a two-way demand valve, a mixing valve and an inverter circulator for radiant panels, plus a dehumidifier connection. Separate communal-space and gym details are shown.
components.design: Apartment inlet 42/38 deg C winter and 13/18 deg C summer; panels 38/33 deg C winter and 18/23 deg C summer.
components.note: Typical communal-space labels of 55/50 deg C differ from the plant's 45/40 deg C branch. The gym detail shows water services; it does not establish a complete HVAC terminal design.

components.name: Rainwater irrigation pump
components.model: DAB MICRA HS 4/4; ACTIVE DRIVER 2.2 or equivalent
components.quantity: 1 pump, in a 3.5 m3 rainwater tank
components.role: Supplies external communal irrigation from rainwater storage; the irrigation arrangement also has a separate groundwater supply connection.
components.note: MICRA HS family sheet downloaded. Actual controller version and changeover logic are unverified. This non-potable circuit remains distinct from drinking-water distribution.

components.name: Fire-water tank filling branch
components.model: No complete fire-system equipment schedule supplied
components.role: Takes mains water to a fire-water tank filling connection.
components.design: 15 m3/h label.
components.note: The drawing does not establish the complete firefighting system, its performance or compliance.

issues.title: Groundwater and cooling temperatures need reconciliation
issues.where: PC2 schedule, magenta source lines, green building lines and SC2 schedule (S00 p.1).
issues.detail: PC2 cooling is selected at 15/10 deg C while its main pipes show 8/13 deg C. Groundwater upstream is annotated 16 deg C, but labels near PC2 include 10 deg C winter / 15 deg C summer inlet. SC2 and distribution returns also differ.
issues.needed: Approved as-built thermal schedule, heat-pump selections and seasonal mixing/control sequence.

issues.title: PC1 efficiency and P05 electrical current differ internally
issues.where: PC1 and P05 equipment schedules (S00 p.1).
issues.detail: PC1 lists 180.5 kW output, 37 kW input and COP 5.00; division gives 4.88. P05 lists 0.75 kW and 11.8 A. These values are retained as source discrepancies.
issues.needed: Original manufacturer selections, nameplates and electrical schedule.

issues.title: Nobel product identity and pressure limits are unresolved
issues.where: T6/T7 schedules (S00), NIC-K PDF p.2 (S13), ML PDF p.2 (S14).
issues.detail: T6 is drawn at 8 bar; candidate NIC 108-K is rated 6 bar. T7 is drawn at 65 m3/h each and 10 W; candidate ML100 gives 60 m3/h and 30 W, with pressure limits by version.
issues.needed: Exact installed series, serial/nameplate data and approved datasheets. Candidate brochures must not be used as substitution approval.

issues.title: Potable-water pressure envelope needs confirmation
issues.where: GP1/GP2, T2 and S2 branches (S00 p.1).
issues.detail: GP1 has both 730 and 930 kPa annotations, while T2 lists maximum 8 bar. Pump head and local equipment pressure are different quantities; suction pressure, reducers and operating conditions matter.
issues.needed: Commissioning pressure schedule, local maximum pressures and installed backflow/reducing-device documentation.

issues.title: Typical terminal temperatures do not all match the plant
issues.where: Communal-space details and Tower B plant branch (S00 p.1).
issues.detail: The typical detail states 55/50 deg C winter and 10/15 deg C summer; the plant branch shows 45/40 deg C winter and 8/13 deg C summer.
issues.needed: Approved terminal selections and final distribution temperature schedule.

issues.title: Control sequence and hygiene plan are missing
issues.where: DDC/cascade notes, T3/T4/T5 and DHW mixing branches (S00 p.1).
issues.detail: Equipment and signals are shown, but priority logic, lead/lag, fault responses, condensation interlocks, chemical specifications and sanitation validation are not supplied.
issues.needed: Control narrative, points list, commissioning records and water-hygiene plan. Confirm the exact K&P controller and PC1/PC2 configurations.

issues.title: Tags and quantities must be read with location
issues.where: Repeated S1/S2/S3/S4, PC2, P01 and restitution-well labels (S00 p.1).
issues.detail: S3 occurs four times across two different loops; PC2 and P01 occur twice. Both restitution-well details are labelled R1. Twin pump symbols describe assemblies, not a verified duty/standby sequence.
issues.needed: Asset register with unique IDs, locations and confirmed duty/standby arrangements.

issues.title: Groundwater permissions and actual installation are unverified
issues.where: Well field and restitution-temperature control (S00 p.1).
issues.detail: The drawing records extraction duties, return conditions and monitoring points; it does not supply abstraction permits, water analyses, environmental limits or evidence of installed equipment.
issues.needed: Well permits, hydrogeological report, water-quality tests and current as-built survey.

glossary: DHW / ACS
Domestic hot water / acqua calda sanitaria.
MR / RR
Supply / return. The source legend uses these for more than one circuit; follow the connection and colour.
AFP / ACP
Cold / hot potable water: acqua fredda / calda potabile.
ACR / RCP
Hot-water recirculation; both labels appear in the drawing.
AFT / AFT-P
Technical water / well-water annotations; these circuits are non-potable.
BP / MP / AP
Low / medium / high pressure. A pressure zone is distinct from a temperature level.
TM / TR
Supply / return temperature. I indicates winter; E indicates summer.
COP / EER
Heating output / electrical input, or cooling output / electrical input, at specified rating conditions. Neither is the seasonal efficiency of the whole plant.
m3/h / kPa / kW
Volume flow / pressure or head / power. Pump head is a pressure increase, not necessarily the system's local pressure.
Buffer / pressure vessel
A thermal buffer adds stored water heat capacity. A pressure vessel uses a compressible gas volume to accommodate pressure/volume changes.
